title: Lichtenwerth Castle Münster
name: Lichtenwerth Castle Münster
kurzbeschreibung: Schloss Lichtenwerth near Münster in the Inntal: a romantic 12th-century medieval moated castle, idyllically situated on the Inn river.
beschreibung:
Overview

The historic Schloss Lichtenwerth is located in the Tyrolean municipality of Münster in the Kufstein district at the entrance to the Zillertal at an altitude of around 525 metres. Originally built on a fortified island within a loop of the Inn river, the estate is considered one of the very few genuine medieval moated castles in Tyrol. Nestled amid ancient riparian forests and manicured meadows, the stately ensemble enchants visitors with its fortified keep, late Gothic battlements, and unmistakable romantic flair.

Architecture & Noble History

The origins of the Veste Lichtenwerth date back to the 12th century, when the Lords of Freundsberg established a fortified stronghold here to control river shipping and the salt trade on the Inn. Over the centuries, the castle changed hands multiple times, belonging among others to the Dukes of Bavaria and the Tyrolean sovereign princes. Following the river regulation of the Inn in the 19th century, the original river loop silted up, leaving the castle surrounded today by an idyllic water-filled moat and castle pond. The architectural fabric blends Romanesque masonry remains with late Gothic residential wings and Baroque living quarters. For several generations, the castle has been privately owned by the count family Grafen Inzaghi, who maintain the heritage-protected landmark with great devotion.

Visit & Location

Because Schloss Lichtenwerth is privately owned and permanently inhabited, the interior rooms and the castle courtyard are generally not open to the public. However, the outer grounds, the romantic castle pond, and the castle park can be wonderfully admired from the surrounding walking and cycling paths. Getting there by car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 (exit Wiesing/Zillertal or Kramsach), taking the regional road to Münster; parking is available in the village centre of Münster. By public transport: ÖBB/S-Bahn to Brixlegg or Jenbach railway station, and from there by bus to Münster.

Tips

The circular trail around the castle and along the Inn riparian wetlands is level and ideal for relaxed family strolls and bike rides on the Inntal-Radweg cycle path. Combine viewing the castle exterior with a trip to neighbouring Rattenberg – Austria's smallest historic town – or to the Reintaler Seen lakes in Kramsach.
